featureRef: 12.18 Termination or dismissal of a member of staff
name: End employment on the school's decision, with notice or immediately, and run the same exit and handover
priorityReason: An immediate termination leaves classes unstaffed the same day, and nothing else releases what the person held.

goal.capability: to end a member of staff's employment on the school's decision and have everything they held handed on
goal.outcome: the decision is recorded and defensible, and no class, section or exam is left without an owner

secondaryActors.involvement: Records the case, serves the notice and works the handover checklist.
Is the subject of it and is notified of the decision and the reason.
Takes over the sections, slots and activities handed on.

preconditions.condition: The employee has an active staff record.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is School Admin or Principal.
The approval configuration is set, or its default applies (BR-2).
A supporting record exists for the case, since a termination with no record cannot be defended (BR-1).

postConditions: The termination is on record with its reason, its supporting record, its approval and its leaving date.
It was approved before it took effect, by whichever role the configuration names, and the Principal's decision is final.
The employee was told the decision, the reason and the leaving date.
The same handover checklist as a resignation was produced and cleared before the leaving date.
Where the effect was immediate, the School Admin worked the checklist rather than the departing employee, and the leaving date was the date of approval.
Access was revoked on the leaving date — login, ID card and biometric enrolment — the same day where the effect was immediate.
The final settlement was calculated on the same basis as a resignation, with any advance recovered or written off with approval.
The staff record was deactivated and not deleted, and the employee dropped out of payroll and the timetable.

dataFields.name: Reason
dataFields.validation: 20 to 2000 characters. Why employment is being ended, in terms that stand up later (BR-1).
dataFields.example: Repeated unauthorised absence after two written warnings, detailed in the attached record.

dataFields.name: Supporting record
dataFields.validation: The warnings, findings or evidence the case rests on. A termination with no record cannot be defended (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Effect
dataFields.validation: With notice, in which case a notice period runs as for a resignation, or with immediate effect (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Notice period
dataFields.validation: Where the effect is with notice. Defaults to the notice period on the staff record.
dataFields.default: The notice period on the record

dataFields.name: Leaving date
dataFields.validation: Produced by the notice period, or the date of approval where the effect is immediate (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Return reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required to return a case unapproved.
dataFields.example: The second warning is not on the record. Attach it before this proceeds.

dataFields.name: Handover worked by
dataFields.validation: The School Admin where the effect is immediate, since the departing employee is gone (BR-5).

dataFields.name: Net settlement
dataFields.validation: Salary to the leaving date, unused leave entitlement, less any advance recovered (BR-7).

businessRules.rule: A termination records the reason and the supporting record it rests on. A decision with no record behind it cannot be defended afterwards.
The case is approved before it takes effect. Who approves is configuration-based; by default it is the Principal, whose decision is final.

The termination is set either with notice, in which case a notice period runs exactly as for a resignation, or with immediate effect, in which case the leaving date is the date of approval and no notice period runs.
The employee is notified of the decision, the reason and the leaving date. A person dismissed without being told why has no way to respond.

The same handover checklist as a resignation is produced — timetable slots, section in charge, unsubmitted marks, activities — and must be cleared before the leaving date. Where the effect is immediate the School Admin works the checklist, since the departing employee is gone.
Access is revoked on the leaving date: login, ID card and biometric enrolment. On an immediate termination this happens the same day.
Accounts calculate the final settlement on the same basis as a resignation — salary to the leaving date, unused leave entitlement, and any outstanding advance recovered or written off with approval.
The staff record is deactivated and never deleted, and the employee drops out of payroll runs and the timetable.
An immediate termination still cannot leave a class unstaffed. The checklist is worked the same day, and anything unassigned is escalated at once rather than over a notice period.
The exit path is the same as a resignation from the handover onward. Only the decision, the approval and the possibility of immediate effect differ.
A termination case is never deleted. A case that is not approved stays on record as returned or withdrawn.
An employee cannot open a termination against themselves or anybody else. Only the School Admin or the Principal can.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → HR → Terminations → Open a termination
basicFlow.userAction: Opens a termination against a member of staff, recording the reason and attaching the supporting record.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires both, since a decision with no record behind it cannot be defended.

basicFlow.userAction: Sets the termination with notice or with immediate effect.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Runs a notice period as for a resignation, or sets the leaving date to the date of approval.

basicFlow.userAction: Approves the case, which is what makes it take effect.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval by whichever role the configuration names. The Principal's decision is final.
Tells the employee the decision, the reason and the leaving date.
Produces the same checklist a resignation produces — timetable slots, section in charge, unsubmitted marks and activities.

basicFlow.userAction: Reassigns each item to a named member of staff, working the checklist themselves where the effect is immediate.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses to let the leaving date pass with anything unassigned, and escalates at once on an immediate termination.
Revokes the login and cancels the ID card and biometric enrolment on the leaving date, the same day where the effect is immediate.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → HR → Final settlement → Calculate → Release
basicFlow.userAction: Calculates and releases the settlement on the same basis as a resignation.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Recovers any advance or writes it off with approval, and deactivates the record without deleting it.

alternateFlows.behaviour: The leaving date is the date of approval, no notice period runs, and the School Admin works the checklist since the departing employee is gone (BR-3, BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: The termination is served with notice
alternateFlows.navigation: Open a termination → Effect → With notice
alternateFlows.behaviour: A notice period runs exactly as for a resignation, and the exit path from the handover onward is identical (BR-3, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The approver does not accept the case
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns with a reason and employment continues. Nothing has been notified and nothing handed over.

alternateFlows.condition: An immediate termination leaves classes unstaffed today
alternateFlows.behaviour: The checklist is worked the same day and anything unassigned is escalated at once rather than over a notice period (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: Marks are unsubmitted for an exam in progress
alternateFlows.behaviour: Responsibility passes to whoever takes the subject over, since the exam cannot be locked without them.

alternateFlows.navigation: Final settlement → Recover advance, or Write off advance
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recovered from the settlement or written off with approval, on the same basis as a resignation (BR-7).

departures.requirement: An immediate termination still cannot leave a class, section or exam subject without an owner. The checklist is worked the same day and escalates at once.
On an immediate termination, login, ID card and biometric enrolment are revoked on the day of approval, not overnight.
No termination can be opened without a reason and a supporting record, by any route.
An approved termination cannot be reversed. Re-employment is a new staff record with a new joining date.
Terminations, their supporting records and their settlements are retained 7 years after exit.

openQuestions.question: Which cases require the Principal's approval and which may the School Admin approve?
openQuestions.assumption: The Principal by default for all. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Is any warning or disciplinary step required before a termination, given performance evaluation is not in MVP?
openQuestions.assumption: Nothing enforces one. The supporting record is the only requirement.

openQuestions.question: Is pay in lieu of notice offered on an immediate termination?
openQuestions.assumption: Not modelled. The settlement runs to the leaving date, which is the approval date.

openQuestions.question: May a terminated employee appeal, and does anything hold the exit while an appeal runs?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The decision is modelled as final.

openQuestions.question: Who works the handover on an immediate termination when the School Admin does not know the subject?
openQuestions.assumption: The School Admin as modelled, with the Coordinator reassigning. Not confirmed.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
